entry.title: SSH Bastion Hosts and Jump Servers: Architecture, ProxyJump, and Zero-Trust Patterns
entry.summary:
Exposing every server directly to the internet is how breaches happen. Here's how to build a hardened single entry point — and then evolve beyond it.
Picture your infrastructure as a building. You wouldn't install a door on every wall and hand out individual keys to every room. You'd build a lobby with a security desk, control who enters, and log every visit. A bastion host is that lobby. It's the single, hardened, publicly accessible server through which all SSH access flows. Every other server in your infrastructure sits behind it — no public IPs, no direct access, no exceptions. entry.title: The Voices Fighting for Digital Freedom: Yanis Varoufakis to Headline Web3 Summit 2026
Google just redesigned the search box for the first time in 25 years — here’s why it matters more than you think.
entry.summary: For a quarter century, the Google search box has been one of the most recognizable interfaces in computing: a thin white rectangle, a blinking cursor, a few typed words, and a list of blue links. On Tuesday, Google will formally retire that paradigm. At its annual I/O developer conference, Google announced a sweeping redesign of the search box itself — the literal text field where billions of queries begin every day — transforming it from a simple keyword input into a dynamic, AI-driven conversation starter that can accept text, images, PDFs, videos, and even open Chrome tabs as inputs.
